title: Angle modes and inverse trig
intro: Use a TI-Nspire CX II-T to find one inverse-trig angle in the unit the question asks for.

beats.spoken: Find the principal angle for sine theta equals zero point six, in degrees. Check the top-right rad or deg label.
beats.coach: The question asks for degrees. Check the mode in the top-right of the calculator screen before you calculate.

beats.spoken: Use the touchpad to move the pointer to rad. Click the touchpad centre. Rad changes to deg.
beats.coach: Move the touchpad pointer to RAD, then click the centre of the touchpad. Check that the label changes to DEG.

beats.spoken: Press trig. Move down to inverse sine and press Enter. The minus one means inverse, not reciprocal.
beats.coach: Press trig, move down to sin⁻¹, then press Enter. Here the exponent notation means inverse sine, not a reciprocal.

beats.spoken: Type zero point six and press Enter. Inverse sine takes a ratio and gives an angle.
beats.coach: Type 0.6 and press Enter. The argument is the ratio, not an angle.

beats.spoken: About thirty-six point eight seven degrees. That is one principal angle. If asked for all solutions, check the whole interval.
beats.coach: The display gives about 36.87° in DEG mode. This is the principal angle. If asked for all solutions, check the full interval.
